title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs (4e mouture)' notes Grothendieck axiomatizes a 'geometric' structure M, a set of 'pieces' (regions, lines, points…). M carries relations: ≤ (being a part), ≪ and its interior variant °≪ (being a part 'in the shadow' of, i.e. non-tangentially contained), a 'compatibility' relation whose negation is written ≭, and the disjointness relations |·| and |°|. From these he defines 'figures' Fig(M), finite configurations of mutually compatible pieces, together with an associated ordered set F̃ (the pieces generated by, or subordinate to, F). On the previous page he studies a map φ: M → M′ satisfying conditions a)–d). Condition d) requires that φ induce a bijection X̃ → X̃′ for every X. From these conditions he derives: (Cor 1) φ maps figures to figures, injectively, as an order-isomorphism; (Cor 2–3) φ preserves and reflects ≤ and ∥ on F̃.

This page continues the list.
- Cor 4: if F, G are figures with F ≭ G (meaning F ∪ G is again a figure), then φ(F) ≭ φ(G), and φ preserves the union F ∪ G and the intersection F ∩ G. Proof: apply Cor 1 to the figure F ∪ G; injectivity there gives preservation of intersections.
- Cor 5: if F ≪ G then φ(F) ≪ φ(G), and the square formed by F̃ → G̃, φ, φ, and F̃′ → G̃′ commutes. So φ is functorial for the 'shadow/subordination' maps between figures.
- Cor 6 (stated only): φ is compatible with the induced operation of 'ajustements' (adjustments) on figures.

Grothendieck then doubts his own axiom. He says he has not grasped the exact meaning of hypothesis d) (transcribed '3)'), which 'seems very strong'. He tests it on the model case φ = inverse image along a continuous map p. There d) appears to force p to be open and surjective, and he notes he has not checked this. A marginal query, with an arrow, asks whether one can see that X |°| Y ⇒ φ(X) |°| φ(Y), i.e. whether φ preserves disjointness.

Example 1: the map M → Figél(M) (elementary figures) sending X ↦ Mutilations(X), the set of mutilations of X. He claims this is an embedding for ≤, ≪ and ≭, and asks what happens for disjointness. He computes the underlying set |Mutilations(X)| = Ombre(X) = M_{≪X} (the shadow of X), and its interior |…|° = Ombre°(X) = M_{°≪X}.

The next page reduces the question to this: is X |°| Y equivalent to {X, Y} having no common °≪-minorant? He finds that it is not in general: two distinct lines x, y have no common minorant but need not be disjoint. Hence whether disjointness is 'induced by' °≪ is an extra 'quasi-set-theoretic' hypothesis on M. The page thus serves to set up the morphisms of these structures, test them on the inverse-image model, and check that the embedding of M into its elementary figures respects all relations.
errors: Cor 4's proof presupposes that F ≭ G means exactly that F ∪ G ∈ Fig(M). That is the natural reading, but it is not restated here.
Preservation of ∩ needs injectivity of φ on F ∪ G (Cor 1). Preservation of ∪ is trivial for images of sets. Both are fine as stated.
Cor 5: the horizontal maps F̃ → G̃ are not defined on this page. Commutativity is asserted without proof.
Cor 6 is only announced; no statement or proof is given.
The analysis of hypothesis d) for inverse images along a continuous map (requiring p open and surjective) is explicitly left unverified ('je n'ai pas vu').
The embedding claim for Example 1 is asserted without proof. Compatibility with |°| is left open here and resolved only partially, negatively in general, on the next page.

ideas.what: Morphisms of 'figure structures' φ: M → M′ that preserve figures, their unions and intersections, and their shadow (≪) maps (Cor 4–6).
ideas.modern_name: Homomorphisms of mereotopological / contact structures; functoriality of a figure-poset construction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mereotopology morphisms: e.g. Düntsch–Winter, Vakarelov (contact algebras, 2000s)
ideas.where_published: Only the general program of 'topologie modérée' appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (1984); not this axiomatics.

ideas.what: Testing the axiom 'φ induces bijections X̃ ≅ X̃′' on the inverse-image functor of a continuous map, where it forces openness/surjectivity.
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of regions along open surjections; preservation of the interior/part-of structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard point-set topology (open maps preserve regular-open structure under preimage)

ideas.what: Embedding X ↦ Mutilations(X) of M into elementary figures, with |Mutilations(X)| = Ombre(X) = M_{≪X} and the interior version Ombre°(X) = M_{°≪X}.
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a region by its down-set of (non-tangential) parts, i.e. a Stone/Priestley-type representation of a mereotopology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone-type representation theorems for contact/region algebras (Düntsch–Winter 2005, Dimov–Vakarelov 2006)

ideas.what: Question whether disjointness |°| is determined by the non-tangential-part relation °≪ (no common °≪-minorant); a counterexample with lines; called a 'quasi-set-theoretic' hypothesis.
ideas.modern_name: Interdefinability of contact/connection C and non-tangential part ≪ in mereotopology

missed.claim: The 1986 Analysis situs notes develop a mereotopology: a calculus of pieces with part-of, non-tangential part ('ombre'), compatibility and disjointness, plus structure-preserving maps. Unlike the Boolean contact algebras of the logic/AI literature, it is designed to include lower-dimensional pieces (lines, points). His example of distinct lines with no common part but not disjoint is precisely where contact and part-of fail to be interdefinable outside the regular-closed, Boolean setting. This link between Grothendieck's tame-topology program and mereotopology/region-based theories of space does not appear in the literature.
missed.quote: le fait que |o| soit induit par °≪ ... une hypothèse de nature "quasi-ensembliste", mais sans conditions particulières aux lignes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a mixed-dimensional mereotopology with a notion of morphism. Such a framework is lacking in region-connection theories and could bridge them to o-minimal / tame geometry.

missed.claim: Two items are left open: what morphism axiom (condition d)) is right so that inverse images along continuous maps qualify, and whether the elementary-figure embedding preserves disjointness. Grothendieck flags d) as too strong; a later marginal note (17.7.86) says it should be weakened.
missed.quote: Je n'ai pas l'impression d'avoir bien saisi le sens exact de l'hypothèse 3), qui semble très forte
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Defining the right category of 'tame spaces' with pullbacks is still a design question for tame-topology foundations. These notes record his attempt, but they are routine in content.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine corollaries about structure-preserving maps. The interest lies in documenting Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic 'analysis situs', which is effectively an independent mixed-dimensional mereotopology, and his explicit doubts about the morphism axiom. No striking finished result appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'l'hypothèse 3)' is very likely 'l'hypothèse d)', referring to condition d) on the previous page.
The marginal formula is likely 'X |°| Y ⇒ φ(X) |°| φ(Y)' (a question about preserving disjointness, with an arrow), not 'φ(X) ⊃ φ(Y), X ⊃ Y'.
Cor 6: 'l'opération d'ajustements induite sur les figures' is a plausible reading of the second line.
The text under Figél(M) reads roughly 'figures élémentaires', which matches the transcription.
